final_message:
I found and fixed six bugs. All 24 tests now pass (8 were failing before), and I didn't change any tests. Some of the bugs weren't covered by the tests, so I also checked those cases by hand against the README.

| File:function | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `amounts.py:parse_amount` | `(45.10)` came out positive: the parentheses were removed but the sign was never applied | Parentheses now make the amount negative |
| `currency.py:minor_units` | It looked up the code in lowercase, but the table uses uppercase, so JPY got 2 decimals instead of 0 | Uses the same uppercase lookup as the rest of the module (this also rejects unknown codes) |
| `currency.py:convert` | The rates were applied backwards: 250 EUR came out as about 231 USD instead of 270 | Now converts A → EUR → B as the README says, rounding once at the end |
| `vat.py:vat_rate_for` | Category names weren't lowercased or trimmed, so `"Food"` or `" books "` got the standard rate | Category names are trimmed and lowercased before the lookup |
| `invoice.py:line_total` | VAT was charged on the amount before the discount | VAT is now charged on the discounted net |
| `dates.py:days_in_range` | Off by one: the end date was left out, and a single-day range came back empty | The end date is now included |

Results from the hand checks:
- 10 USD → JPY gives 1481 (whole yen).
- `-0.005` rounds to `-0.01`.
- `-$12.50`, `$-12.50` and `($1,200.00)` all parse as negative.

I made one extra change inside `parse_amount`. Once parentheses made the amount negative, `(-5)` would have parsed as positive `5.00`, so it now raises `ValueError`. I counted this as part of the parentheses bug rather than a separate line in the report.

Two things I looked at and left alone:
- **Comma placement:** `1,2,3` is still accepted and read as `123`. The README doesn't say how strict to be, so I didn't tighten it.
- **Float inputs:** `convert` and `vat_amount` still accept floats and turn them into imprecise decimals. The README says money is always `Decimal`, so I didn't treat this as a bug.

`REPORT.md` has one line per bug in the format you asked for.
